summary.headline: Supreme Industries H1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 31% to Rs 487 crore on 22% value growth, but volume grew only about 1%; FY27 volume growth guided at about 10%.
summary.overview: H1 FY27 sales volume was 341,991 MT (up about 1% YoY) and revenue from operations was Rs 6,079 crore (up 22%). Standalone operating profit rose 34% to Rs 829 crore and PAT rose 31% to Rs 487 crore. Q2 showed a sharp rebound in Plastic Piping (volume +24%, value +42%), while Consumer Products and Packaging lagged on polymer price volatility. Management cut company-wide FY27 volume growth guidance to about 10% and reiterated a 14% to 14.5% operating margin for the full year.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 580 crore last year as stated by CFO; Q1 employee cost stated as Rs 168 crore, up 25% YoY
analyst cited; below management's full-year 14% to 14.5% guidance

segments.name: Plastic Piping Systems
segments.commentary: Q2 volume +24% and value +42% YoY; H1 volume growth about 2%. Q1 volume had fallen about 13.5%. Growth mainly from housing; October-to-date (about 25 days) volume growth 23%.

segments.name: Packaging
segments.commentary: Q2 volume +3% and value +22% YoY. Margins contracted as polythene and polypropylene costs rose and packaging film prices could not be raised quickly.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Q2 volume +13% and value +49% YoY. No volume guidance given; custom moulding for industrial customers.

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Q2 volume -14% and value +2% YoY. Pressure from polypropylene availability and price; furniture made from polypropylene.

segments.name: Others (incl. PVC windows & doors, raw material trading)
segments.commentary: Others revenue rose from about Rs 20 crore to about Rs 80 crore, per analyst question; includes PVC windows & doors and surplus raw material sales. MOHO bath fittings sit within Plastic Piping.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company-wide volume growth guided at about 10%, reduced from earlier levels after Q1 de-growth.
FY27 piping volume growth guided at 13%, cut from 15% and then 17%; H2 would require roughly 22% growth over H1 per analyst math.
FY27 revenue of Rs 13,500 crore to Rs 14,000 crore for Supreme Industries standalone, per Chairman.
FY27 operating margin guided at 14% to 14.5%.
FY27 capex cash outflow not to exceed Rs 700 crore to Rs 750 crore, funded through internal accruals.
Inventory gains expected to be recognised in H1 overall; final figure at year-end close in March 2027.
capex_capacity: New units under work at Bihar, Jammu, Erode, Puducherry and Malanpur, plus brownfield expansion at various sites, progressing as planned.
Composite cylinder utilisation improving gradually as procurement has begun at all three Oil Marketing Companies.
Gas pipe fittings now supplied from five locations (East, West, South, North, Northeast).
Capacity described as ample across multiple sites; most orders delivered within 48 hours.
Employee cost increase partly reflects new units not present in H1 last year; no new greenfield expected in H2, so H1 employee cost is the H2 benchmark (excluding director commission).
demand_pricing: Management says the Q2 piping growth came mainly from housing; agriculture expected to contribute for the full year.
PVC prices rose in October and cPVC price hike announced effective 1 November, around 3% to 7% by product; management says customers can absorb it.
Price increases passed on with a lag of about 10 to 15 days, which management said helps distributors repair their balance sheets.
Industry PVC volume in H1 FY27 de-grew about 10%, per raw material producer data (Chairman).
CPVC volume grew 38.5% in H1 FY27.
Nal Se Jal orders expected to be much lower than budget this year; management does not expect a large contribution.
Polypropylene prices high; Middle East polythene supply disrupted, making packaging price pass-through difficult.

qa_highlights.question: Does the cut to 13% piping growth look achievable, and could it be cut again?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said no further cut is expected, citing about 23% volume growth in October to date (25 days), adequate capacity and raw material cover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall in Q2 and what drives recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated FY27 margin guidance of 14% to 14.5%; CFO cited high raw material prices; packaging margins hit by inability to pass on polythene costs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said outflow should not exceed Rs 700 to 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 13,500 crore to Rs 14,000 crore revenue and 14% to 14.5% operating margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is Supreme gaining share at the expense of unorganised players?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said Supreme's market share grew YoY while the industry declined about 10% in H1, per raw material producer data.

qa_highlights.question: What is full-year employee cost?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H1 employee cost was Rs 330 crore versus Rs 580 crore last year; H1 level used as H2 benchmark.

risks_watch: Piping volume growth guidance of 13% needs about 22% H2 growth over H1, per analyst math; watch October-December volume print.
Margins below the 14% to 14.5% full-year guidance in Q1 and Q2; packaging and consumer margins under pressure.
Crude and polymer volatility, West Asia geopolitics, and rupee depreciation raising imported raw material costs.
Consumer products volume down 14% in Q2 on polypropylene availability and government-driven diversion to LPG.
Nal Se Jal government-funded orders weak; state fund matching and unpaid bills delay recovery.
Inventory gains and channel inventory levels; customers keeping inventory at minimum.
summary.management_tone: Confident on piping volume momentum and October trends, but cautious on the wider macro. Management was defensive when pressed on margin shortfall and packaging pricing, and gave indirect answers on inventory gains and price pass-through.
key_quotes: Going at the present situation, we do not expect any lower number to be announced again.
We have given volume growth of 13% in the piping business.
We are very comfortable at 14%, 14.5% we get a very good return on our investment.
Nal Se Jal this year as on today, I can say it is going to be much lower than what was the budget.

adds.what: New units under work at Bihar, Jammu, Erode, Puducherry and Malanpur, plus brownfield expansion at various sites

growth.why: FY27 company-wide volume growth cut to about 10% and piping volume to 13%, with H1 volume only about +1%, so H2 needs a sharp pickup; backing rests on new units at five sites (no commissioning dates given) and Q2 piping rebound, while the 14-14.5% margin guide was held.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management held FY27 operating margin guidance at 14% to 14.5% but Q2 margin was about 13% (analyst cited) and H1 operating profit rose 34% on revenue up 22%, so H2 needs margin expansion; packaging margins are squeezed as polythene costs rose faster than price pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New units under work at Bihar, Jammu, Erode, Puducherry and Malanpur plus brownfield expansion, with no commissioning dates given; utilisation not quantified, but management calls capacity ample, so timing is unclear.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 volume was only about +1% (341,991 MT) and FY27 company-wide volume guidance was cut to about 10%, so H2 needs a sharp pickup; piping October-to-date volume is +23% over about 25 days, but piping guidance of 13% implies about 22% H2 growth over H1 per analyst math.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex outflow was cut to Rs 700 to 750 crore, funded from internal accruals, and no new greenfield is expected in H2, pointing away from fresh capex announcements.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Company-wide volume guidance was cut to about 10% and piping to 13%, with H1 volume about +1%; margin guidance was only held, not raised, against a Q2 margin near 13%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Chairman says no further piping cut is expected, but H2 piping needs about 22% growth over H1 and Q2 margin of about 13% sits below the 14% to 14.5% full-year guide; packaging and consumer products are under pressure from polymer costs.

rows.label: cPVC and PVC price hikes passed through
rows.why: cPVC price hike of about 3% to 7% by product effective 1 November after PVC rose in October; management says customers can absorb it, with pass-through lagging 10 to 15 days.

rows.label: Share gains against unorganised players
rows.why: Supreme's market share grew YoY while industry PVC volume fell about 10% in H1 FY27; CPVC volume grew 38.5% in H1.

rows.label: Nal Se Jal government orders weak
rows.why: Orders expected to be much lower than budget this year, with state fund matching and unpaid bills delaying recovery, so management does not expect a large contribution.

tone.note: Management was confident on piping momentum (October-to-date volume +23%) and no further piping cut, but defensive on the Q2 margin shortfall and packaging price pass-through; analysts pressed on whether H2 volume and the 14-14.5% margin guide are achievable.
